name: Craftsman Automation Ltd
title: Craftsman Automation Ltd - 543276 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Craftsman guides FY27 revenue growth to mid-teens, with alloy wheel exit run-rate near 3 million wheels a year and net debt/EBITDA at 2.43x.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of heavy capex that is now being absorbed, with the alloy wheel ramp at Bhiwadi and Hosur reaching a March exit run-rate of about 3 million wheels annualised against 5.5 million capacity. Sunbeam (aluminium) is being restructured through exits of unprofitable customers, product lines and a roughly INR30 crore low-value line sale, with benefits expected from Q2 FY27. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to mid-teens, conditional on aluminium prices holding near current levels. Rising manpower and capex costs were the main concerns, with the Gurgaon land sale and the DR Axion land deal also discussed.

financial_highlights.value: around INR280 crore (management unsure, floated INR240 crore)

financial_highlights.change: Expected below 2x in current year, then about 1.5x

financial_highlights.value: INR3,100 crore (about INR2,700 crore excluding Gurgaon land sale)

financial_highlights.change: Same as last year, per analyst

financial_highlights.value: about INR400 crore in FY25 and INR600 crore in FY26

segments.name: Powertrain
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation around 65-70%, with an upper limit of 85%. Large-engine new powertrain business is not yet meaningful (under 0.5% of powertrain revenue) and is expected to reach only low single-digit share in FY27, rising to high single digit in FY28, with traction in FY29-FY30. Stationary engine order book of first $100 million is finalised, with revenue targeted in FY29-FY30.

segments.name: Aluminium (Craftsman, DR Axion, Sunbeam)
segments.commentary: Management targets $1 billion revenue in 2-3 years, with an approximate FY27 aluminium revenue of INR6,500 crore (not guidance). DR Axion utilisation about 80-85% with a new Sriperumbudur plant due for commissioning by December. Sunbeam utilisation of about 70% will fall to 45-50% as legacy lines are exited.

segments.name: Alloy wheels
segments.commentary: Capacity around 5.5 million wheels, with FY27 exit rate expected near 4 million (70-80% utilisation). Bhiwadi margins expected at high single to double digit EBIT, Hosur at single digit while ramping. Phase 2 expansion deferred, with decision after FY26.

segments.name: Industrial engineering
segments.commentary: Smaller segment, described as backbone for powertrain and aluminium. Racks and ASRS systems supplied to automotive battery storage, with possible data-centre and battery-plant opportunities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to mid-teens (double-digit), assuming aluminium prices stay near current levels; commodity moves could inflate or deflate the top line.
Sunbeam margin improvement expected from Q2 FY27 after restructuring, with capacity utilisation falling to 45-50%.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 2x in FY27 and about 1.5x afterwards.
Powertrain double-digit growth expected; Phase 2 powertrain capex decision by September 2026 based on order inflow.
FY27 capex not yet fixed; to be decided in September. Capex cost is expected to be about 1.5x higher in future years.
capex_capacity: Alloy wheel capacity about 5.5 million wheels; no further stretch decision in FY27.
Powertrain capacity utilisation around 60% including new large-engine lines; Phase 1 capacity being completed at foundry and machining sites, with Phase 2 pending order inflow.
DR Axion greenfield plant at Sriperumbudur on about 50 acres (land cost about INR150 crore, acquired via two subsidiaries) to be commissioned by December 2026.
Management is weighing a separate Chennai campus for Craftsman high-pressure die casting, with DR Axion expansion to follow.
Sunbeam land sale put up for sale; buyers are asking discounts of about 15% below market, though management is holding out for a higher price.
demand_pricing: Aluminium: exiting unprofitable customers and sub-segments; insisting on aluminium price pass-through, and declining to supply where it is not available. Legacy product prices being reset rather than increased.
Export inquiries rising for 4-wheeler aluminium components in Europe and North America.
Data-centre and AI demand cited as a positive for Indian manufacturing; capacity is full at many peers.
Domestic farm powertrain improving; truck segment muted. Export of some truck engine blocks will continue rather than be discontinued.
Alloy wheel imports: competitive risk after BIS norms settle, being monitored.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to mid-teens growth (double-digit), conditional on aluminium prices staying near current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did powertrain margins spike, and will they sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the end of about four to five quarters of repair and maintenance costs, manpower reduction through automation, and new products at newer prices, not scale. Scale benefits are expected in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outflow of INR400 crore in FY25 and INR600 crore in FY26: one-off or ongoing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to ramp-up of the aluminium business and that payment cycles are now set, with no big change expected.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and debt reduction plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex not yet fixed and will be decided in September. Management is tracking net debt/EBITDA and ROCE rather than absolute debt; ROCE is 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Powertrain about 65-70% (60% including large-engine lines), alloy wheel exit rate near 3 million on 5.5 million capacity, DR Axion 80-85%, Sunbeam 70% falling to 45-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for consolidating aluminium entities and the DR Axion land deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation targets synergies and shared customers; DR Axion acquired about 50 acres through subsidiaries at about INR150 crore after SIPCOT could not provide land on time.

risks_watch: Aluminium price pass-through: failure would hurt margins and revenue, given management's warning against lead-lag.
Manpower cost inflation expected to run about 20% a year, versus 5-10% earlier, and hard to pass on to customers; labour code and minimum wage resets.
Sunbeam margins still single-digit; restructuring benefits from Q2 FY27 to be verified.
Working capital intensity after FY25-FY26 outflows of INR400-600 crore per year.
Large-engine powertrain revenue is minimal; FY28-FY30 traction is unproven.
Sunbeam land sale timing uncertain, with buyers asking discounts.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the growth outlook and aluminium scale ambitions, but cautious and at times evasive on capex quantum, aluminium margin timing and FY27 capex, which are deferred to September. Management was most candid about the inflationary pressure from manpower, energy and consumables costs.
key_quotes: It is truly double digit, most probably, in the mid-teens, I would say.
The customers who are exiting also need some time to find other suppliers.
We are continuously monitoring the net debt to EBITDA as the monitor to bring it down.
What is worrying us the inflationary manpower cost, which is very difficult to pass on to customer.

adds.what: DR Axion greenfield aluminium plant at Sriperumbudur (about 50 acres)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth to mid-teens (double digit), conditional on aluminium prices holding; backing is partial, citing the DR Axion Sriperumbudur plant (due December 2026), Sunbeam restructuring and pass-through pricing, but no quantified order book supports it.
